note: Explicit event connections, in narrative order. Lines connect named reference points and do not claim exact historical tracks. River routes use the local river geometry between reference points.

AHOM-001.caption: Sukaphaa’s journey overview · 1215–1253. Approximate connections from Mong Mao through the Patkai / Pangsau reference, Namrup and early settlements to Charaideo. Intermediate stages are omitted; the lines are not a surveyed itinerary. Use the reading path to follow individual stages.

sources.title: Dimbeswar Neog, Introduction to Assam, p. 67
N. K. Basu, Assam in the Ahom Age, migration and settlements

AHOM-006.caption: Approach to Assam, 1215–1228. Mong Mao → Patkai / Pangsau reference → Namrup. Approximate connections; intermediate stops and the precise mountain track are not reconstructed.

AHOM-011.caption: Arrival in the Namrup region, 1228. The line links the catalogue’s pass and settlement references; it is not an exact trail.

AHOM-012.caption: Settlement phase, following arrival in 1228 and before Charaideo in 1253. A simplified sequence of named places; intermediate settlements are omitted and the scene’s displayed date does not cover the entire sequence.

AHOM-017.caption: The final settlement connection to Charaideo, established as Sukaphaa’s capital in 1253. Reference points are approximate.

AHOM-065.caption: The prince returns from Habung to Charaideo. The connection follows the Brahmaputra between nearby river reference points.

AHOM-095.caption: The Sadiya area provides a reference for the Chutia campaign; the precise march is not plotted.

AHOM-113.caption: Retreat from the capital toward Namrup, shown as a connection between the named places.

AHOM-131.caption: The invasion advances along the Brahmaputra. This account does not specify a complete itinerary.

AHOM-134.caption: Namrup and the occupied capital locate the counter-war; no single battle position is asserted.

AHOM-209.caption: Gaurinath's flight down the Brahmaputra, from the Rangpur region toward Guwahati.

AHOM-215.caption: The account names Jorhat as the destination. The invasion's exact Patkai pass and march are not reconstructed.

AHOM-241.caption: The Kachari capital shifts from Dimapur to Maibong after the campaign. The line connects the two capitals.

AHOM-250.caption: The westward advance from Guwahati toward Dhubri, linked along the Brahmaputra.

AHOM-258.caption: Rudra Singha moves from Rangpur toward the Guwahati camp. The projected Bengal campaign remains unlaunched.

AHOM-270.caption: The court moves from Rangpur to Jorhat. The connection marks the change of capital.

AHOM-274.caption: Jorhat is the regional reference for Mahgarh; the retreat ends at Guwahati. The exact battlefield is not pinned.

AHOM-276.caption: Gomdhar's supporters advance from near Jorhat toward Rangpur. The line connects the places named in the account.
